text: A two-day-old infant with bilious vomiting, failure to pass meconium, and abdominal distension is a medical emergency; was the baby born via a Cesarean section or was there any meconium-stained amniotic fluid prior to delivery?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung's disease.

The clinical presentation of bilious vomiting, failure to pass meconium, and abdominal distension in a 2-day-old infant is classic for intestinal obstruction; I have requested an abdominal X-ray to confirm the findings and rule out other causes like meconium ileus.
